In 1812, one man commanded an empire stretching from Spain to Poland by conquering it soldier by soldier.

Today, military power looks completely different — then vs now, a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ At its peak, Napoleon's France directly ruled or controlled through allies and satellites most of continental Europe — Spain, Italy, the Confederation of the Rhine, the Grand Duchy of Warsaw — all answering to Paris.

2/ Building that empire took decades of war and needed hundreds of thousands of men marched across the continent. The 1812 invasion of Russia alone deployed roughly 600,000 troops — most never came home.

3/ Fast forward to today: this map shows armed forces personnel by country. China, India and the US field the largest militaries by headcount — each with over a million active personnel.

Data: Our World in Data (CC BY)

4/ Raw numbers mislead, though. Per capita, small states like North Korea, Israel and Eritrea maintain some of the largest militaries relative to population — a legacy of conscription and permanent threat, not conquest.
5/ Napoleon's map was drawn by armies moving borders. Today's map is mostly drawn by armies that stay inside their own — the largest forces on Earth now exist to deter war, not expand territory.

6/ Same continent, same instinct to measure power in soldiers — just a completely different map of what that power is for.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
